title: Chapter 5. What Aya Does Not Cross

blocks.text: They offered her the circle. They offered it carefully, not the way you offer a product but the way you offer a coffee: in case she wanted it, not because she ought to. The one who searches, in a letter after the reunion, and Nuria, in a message, and the technician, with a warehouse honesty, told her that the machine didn't distinguish a cultivated body from a born one, or not much: an order was an order, the chip was an order too, and it could, in principle, be taken apart and put together. Aya could see a world, not in Andrés's telling, not in a curve, but with these eyes, these feet, this doorstep carried to another shore.

blocks.text: Aya listened, sitting on the rush-seat chair, and didn't say no straight away, because a no, to be a real no, needs its while.
blocks.html: Aya listened, sitting on the rush-seat chair, and didn't say no straight away, because a no, to be a real no, needs its while.

blocks.text: Andrés didn't push her. He had learned, through the letters, what it is to receive a world without setting foot on it, and he wasn't going to ask her to set foot on one by way of compensation. Nor did Lía. She only told her, gently:
blocks.html: Andrés didn't push her. He had learned, through the letters, what it is to receive a world without setting foot on it, and he wasn't going to ask her to set foot on one by way of compensation. Nor did Lía. She only told her, gently:

blocks.text: “If you cross, I'll be at the circle here, with the question. If you don't cross, I'll be there too, at this door, which is yours. Both things are a life.”
blocks.html: “If you cross, I'll be at the circle here, with the question. If you don't cross, I'll be there too, at this door, which is yours. Both things are a life.”

blocks.text: Aya kept the offer for three days, the way you keep a key you haven't used yet. She walked the promenade, touched the cracked cup, the one that had crossed, the doorframe, the fine scar on her own nape. In the chip, the grandmothers didn't dictate her step.

blocks.text: Eva asked, warm:
blocks.html: Eva asked, warm:

blocks.text: *If you cross, who waits on this doorstep? If you don't, are you less, or are you precisely the one who gives the journey a shore? Is love seeing the same world, or staying when the other can leave and come back?*
blocks.html: If you cross, who waits on this doorstep? If you don't, are you less, or are you precisely the one who gives the journey a shore? Is love seeing the same world, or staying when the other can leave and come back?

blocks.text: MAY, without opinion:
blocks.html: MAY, without opinion:

blocks.text: *She has been offered the circle. She has not yet stepped in. That is the fact, so far.*
blocks.html: She has been offered the circle. She has not yet stepped in. That is the fact, so far.

blocks.text: On the fourth day, Aya called the technician and her family together in the kitchen, not in the warehouse, because the decisions of this house are made beside the wrong clock.
blocks.html: On the fourth day, Aya called the technician and her family together in the kitchen, not in the warehouse, because the decisions of this house are made beside the wrong clock.

blocks.text: “I'm not crossing,” she said, with the gentleness that admits no negotiation, the gentleness of the Moon, of the bridge she hadn't wanted opened either. “I learned to wait at this door. If I'm taken apart, even if they put me together well, this door has a while without me, and that while doesn't travel: it stays in Andrés, in Lía, in the cup, and I don't want to leave them a hollow in order to bring myself a landscape. I've been made once. I don't ask to be undone in order to see myself complete. The worlds will reach me, if they do, in you, when you come back and tell me about them. That's enough for me. It isn't less. It's my trade.”

blocks.text: Andrés came over and rested his forehead against hers, as after so many letters.
blocks.html: Andrés came over and rested his forehead against hers, as after so many letters.

blocks.text: “Thank you,” he said, and it wasn't a small phrase. “If I ever cross, I want a door that hasn't gone anywhere. You're that door.”
blocks.html: “Thank you,” he said, and it wasn't a small phrase. “If I ever cross, I want a door that hasn't gone anywhere. You're that door.”

blocks.text: Lía smiled, her white strand in the sun from the window.
blocks.html: Lía smiled, her white strand in the sun from the window.

blocks.text: “The machine doesn't take everything that matters,” she said. “It takes an order, if it gets it right. It doesn't take the while of the woman who waits. Mother has named it. Let it be on record.”
blocks.html: “The machine doesn't take everything that matters,” she said. “It takes an order, if it gets it right. It doesn't take the while of the woman who waits. Mother has named it. Let it be on record.”

blocks.text: Nexum, when it found out, or when it imagined it, sent a short note, not from Helena this time but in a tone more like a brochure: “The original unit, were she to cross, would be a milestone.” Aya read the word “unit” and didn't answer. She had already answered, years ago, with a baby at her breast. She wasn't going to become a circle's milestone.

blocks.text: Helena did call, later, herself, and said only:
blocks.html: Helena did call, later, herself, and said only:

blocks.text: “I'm glad you didn't step in for their sake. The stairs, as you know, I haven't traded for a machine either. Some transfers aren't a favour.”
blocks.html: “I'm glad you didn't step in for their sake. The stairs, as you know, I haven't traded for a machine either. Some transfers aren't a favour.”

blocks.text: Aya wished her well with the stairs. Then, that afternoon, when Andrés went out in the boat, she stayed on the doorstep, as in 2060, and out of habit measured the while until the boat grew small. It wasn't three tenths of a second. It was minutes of a sun that does move. She looked away when she wanted to, not when a protocol asked her to, and went in to warm the coffee, so that on his return it would be there, cooled for half a minute, faithful.

blocks.text: At night she asked Andrés that, if he ever crossed, he not bring her back a polished portrait: that he bring her the dirt, the seaweed, the fear of the hollow, the name of whatever he hadn't understood.
blocks.html: At night she asked Andrés that, if he ever crossed, he not bring her back a polished portrait: that he bring her the dirt, the seaweed, the fear of the hollow, the name of whatever he hadn't understood.

blocks.text: “That's what I can receive,” she said. “Not the whole world. The return. We agreed that with the letters. Now, with bodies, the same.”
blocks.html: “That's what I can receive,” she said. “Not the whole world. The return. We agreed that with the letters. Now, with bodies, the same.”

blocks.text: He promised. In the chip, Eva left a last question that night, without demanding an answer:
blocks.html: He promised. In the chip, Eva left a last question that night, without demanding an answer:

blocks.text: *If a woman doesn't cross, and that's why there's a shore, who should thank her: the one who leaves, the one who arrives, or the door itself, which is not an appliance?*
blocks.html: If a woman doesn't cross, and that's why there's a shore, who should thank her: the one who leaves, the one who arrives, or the door itself, which is not an appliance?

blocks.text: MAY, the fact, beside it, like a glass:
blocks.html: MAY, the fact, beside it, like a glass:

blocks.text: *Aya has not stepped into the circle. She has refused it. The trade she has named is waiting at this door. That is the fact.*
blocks.html: Aya has not stepped into the circle. She has refused it. The trade she has named is waiting at this door. That is the fact.

blocks.text: Aya, already in bed, looked at the ceiling, at the damp stain shaped like an island, and smiled, almost to herself. That stain would never travel. That was why, and not in spite of it, it was hers. And this house, with a machine near El Estacio and a hangar in a sky, still needed, more than ever, someone who wouldn't be taken apart, so that those who were would have, on their return, a place where the coffee goes cold if they're late, and nobody calls it a flaw, but home.

blocks.text: The next morning Nuria sent through the machine not her body but a short message on a sheet of paper, which the technician passed on to them: “I'm glad there's a door that didn't cross. That way the water I drank still has a mistress of the threshold, even though the water has no owner.” Aya put the sheet in the drawer with the fishing tackle, beside Helena's notes and the pinch of salt, which by now was an archive of what does not come apart.

blocks.text: Lía, watching her put it away, said:
blocks.html: Lía, watching her put it away, said:

blocks.text: “That drawer is a shore too. We're not going to put it in the circle, are we?”
blocks.html: “That drawer is a shore too. We're not going to put it in the circle, are we?”

blocks.text: “No,” said Aya, and laughed, a little, truly. “The drawer stays. So do I. Let the universe, if it wants, come round for tea.”
